q: Why is ROAS increasing while net profit is declining?

checks.what: tool: ROAS attempted or derived from its definition

answer:
ROAS is up, but your premise is wrong — Net ROAS rose while Net Profit also improved (became less negative), not declined.

Evidence (measured)
- Net ROAS (order-date): 0.74x → 0.97x (+31%). Measured.
- Net profit (order-date): ₹-5,32,557 → ₹-28,490 (NET LOSS reduced by ₹5,04,067). Measured.
Key drivers (measured)
- Ad spend (order/P&L basis): ₹20,69,132 → ₹10,02,451 (−52%) — lower spend raised ROAS. Measured.
- Contribution margin: ₹15,36,575 → ₹9,73,961 (−37%) — margin fell, which pulled profit down compared with what it might have been. Measured.
- Net sales (P&L basis): ₹26,46,302 → ₹16,29,235 (−38%). Measured.

What this means (measured + arithmetic)
- ROAS rose mainly because ad spend dropped much faster than contribution margin did (ad spend −52% vs margin −37%), so margin per rupee of spend improved — that increases ROAS. Measured + Derived.
- Net profit improved because the reduction in ad spend (the largest cash outflow reducing losses) more than offset the fall in contribution margin, moving net profit toward zero. Measured + Derived.

Context: Period compared = 2026-09-15..2026-10-13 vs 2026-08-16..2026-09-14 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-14.
